text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000163 bills 99215 far above expectation in every complexity group, but the few charts returned support the billed levels, so the pattern cannot yet be called upcoding or a sicker panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess 99215 share is not limited to complex patients: in the by-complexity table it is several times the all-provider share even for patients with 0 or 1 conditions, and sampled low-complexity 99215s such as C0078036 (J06.9 only) and C0078001 (Z09 only) look hard to square with high complexity, though the high-complexity sample (e.g., C0078027, C0078119) fits the billed level. Against that, all 7 documented 99215s were supported, but 7 charts is too few to clear an excess this large. The supporting notes also raise questions: C0078017, a single-condition diabetes visit documented at high MDM, is also flagged on the problems note check, one in five returned notes was flagged as duplicate, and no audit trail was received, so cloned or inflated notes cannot be ruled out. A reviewer should first request charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet, along with the EHR audit trail, and compare those notes for templated or duplicated content before weighing the documentation as support."}
